tldr: Midday batch (Sep 4): GPT-6 Astra's API pricing is live at $10/$50 per MTok with a $1 cached-input rate — but prompts over 272K input tokens trigger 2x/1.5x multipliers on the whole request, a real budgeting trap for long-context agents. A new armature.tech study measured which tools Claude, Codex and Cursor actually install across 17k sandboxed runs (they agree only 42% of the time). Qwen released E-Commerce Bench (365-day autonomous storefronts run against fraudsters and real economics), Google open-sourced TimesFM-3 for native multivariate forecasting, and ik_llama.cpp merged MTP support that doubles Qwen3.8-Flash-Next to 90 tok/s on a 5090. LessWrong digs into Astra's recurrent architecture, while two HF papers explore self-evolving agent harnesses (HarnessDev) and distilling GitHub repos into agent skills (Repo-To-Skill).

articles.title: GPT-6 Astra API pricing lands: $10/$50 per MTok
articles.summary: Astra at $10 in / $50 out per MTok, $1 cached — but >272K input tokens bill 2x/1.5x on the whole request. 1.05M context, 128K max output.

articles.title: Which tools do Claude, Codex and Cursor choose? 17k runs measured
articles.summary: 16,893 sandboxed sessions, 75 repos: agents agree on a tool only 42% of the time. Claude Code web-searches least but reads 3x more pages when it does.

articles.title: Qwen's E-Commerce Bench: agents run stores for 365 days
articles.summary: Long-horizon business benchmark: agents start with ¥100,000, run online stores for a year — sourcing, pricing, inventory, 152 fraudsters among suppliers.

articles.title: Google releases TimesFM-3 for native multivariate forecasting
articles.summary: TimesFM-3 is a 330M-param time-series foundation model handling multiple targets and covariates natively (vs single-series in 2.5); non-commercial license.

articles.title: ik_llama.cpp merges MTP: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next doubles to 90 tok/s
articles.summary: Multi-token prediction now on main in ik_llama.cpp (PR #2369) — 45 → 90 tok/s on a 5090 + 128GB, still usable down to a 12GB 4070.

articles.title: How concerned should we be about Astra's recurrent architecture?
articles.summary: LessWrong thread (103 pts, 61 comments) on safety and interpretability implications of Astra's recurrent design vs standard transformer stacks.

articles.title: HarnessDev: can LLMs create and evolve their own agent harnesses?
articles.summary: New HF paper (2609.01437) on self-improving agent scaffolding — models generating and iterating on their own harness code rather than using fixed tooling.

articles.title: Repo-To-Skill: distilling GitHub repositories into agent skills
articles.summary: DisCo distilled 1,000 ML repos into 5,000+ verified skills — the same agent scores +134% on MLE-bench with skills vs without.
